record.title: Profile logo URL fetched server-side without destination restriction when rendering document PDFs (blind SSRF)
record.description: A user holding ProfileInformation:Write on a company profile can store an arbitrary URL string as the profile logo resource. The only validation is url.Parse, which accepts any string. When a shipment document is built, the admin or seller logo URL becomes SourceDoc.Info.Logo. GET /docs/pdf then renders the document in the API process. docpdf.header treats any value starting with 'http' as a logo URL and calls LogoCache.fetch. That fetch uses http.DefaultClient (NewLogoCache(nil)), which has no scheme, host, IP-range or redirect restriction. The result is an authenticated, blind, GET-only server-side request to any host the API process can reach, with a 15s timeout. The response is not returned to the caller. A non-image or non-200 response draws nothing. A 5xx response surfaces as an error. The only visible effect is that a response that decodes as an image is embedded in the rendered PDF. Impact is limited by the GET-only method, the lack of attacker-chosen headers, the lack of a response channel for non-images, and the likely IAM or authentication requirements on internal services. io.ReadAll on the response body is unbounded, so a large response could cause memory pressure. Whether the render host can reach valuable unauthenticated internal HTTP targets is a deployment fact that cannot be settled from source.
record.claimed_root_cause: User-controlled logo URL is validated only by url.Parse and later fetched by LogoCache.fetch with an unrestricted http.Client, with no allow-list of hosts or schemes (for example the upload bucket or CDN), no blocking of private or link-local IPs, and no response size limit.

trace.scope: company profile form save (profileLogo case), reachable by users with ProfileInformation Write (editProfile at line 67)
trace.description: The profileLogo field value is parsed with field.ParseValidURLs. The URLs are stored at line 705 as ap.Resources[administrator.RscLogo].
Each delimited value is checked only with url.Parse, which accepts nearly any string. No scheme or host check is applied.
The admin profile's first logo URL, or the seller's logo URL for seller shipments (lines 316-319), is returned as doc.Info.Logo (assigned at lines 171 and 302).
Any logo string starting with 'http' is classified logoDoc and passed to opts.Logos.logo(ctx, info.Logo).

c.client.Do(req) issues a GET to the attacker-supplied URL using http.DefaultClient (handler.go line 48, NewLogoCache(nil)). The body is read in full at line 114 and decoded with image.DecodeConfig at line 118.

evidence.description: Only url.Parse is checked for logo URLs.
A nil client falls back to http.DefaultClient with no dialer, redirect or IP restrictions.
PDFHandler constructs the cache with NewLogoCache(nil). The handler is authenticated via AuthHTTP (line 58), and the document resolves through the caller's own authorization.

Only status 200 proceeds. 5xx returns an error that is surfaced to the caller (limited error oracle). Other statuses return an empty result. Non-images draw nothing, so there is no response-body exfiltration for non-image content.

blockers: Egress and reachability facts are not in source: whether the API/docs process can reach internal HTTP services that are unauthenticated or lack a Metadata-Flavor-style header requirement.
Which roles hold ProfileInformation Write on seller and admin profiles in production, and whether those are external lower-trust tenants or only staff.
Source shows no response channel beyond image embedding in the PDF and a 5xx error oracle, so the value of the SSRF depends on deployment network layout.

validation_plan.local: In a dev environment with synthetic data only, set a logo on a test seller profile to a URL on a local listener that logs requests. Render a shipment document through GET /docs/pdf and confirm one GET arrives from the API process. Then point the logo at a local image served by that listener and confirm it is embedded. Also confirm a non-image response and a non-200 response draw no logo. Confirm that no private-IP block exists on the client.
validation_plan.deployment: Owner check: review the Cloud Run service egress and VPC connector or firewall configuration for the API service and list any internal HTTP endpoints reachable without authentication. Review the profile-permission role assignments to see whether external sellers hold ProfileInformation Write. Optionally query stored logo resources for URLs pointing to non-upload hosts. Do not probe live.

separate_root_causes: LogoCache.fetch reads the full response body with io.ReadAll with no size cap (memory-exhaustion DoS by an authenticated profile editor), distinct from the SSRF root cause.
